prompt: Write an email to my landlord asking to fix a leaking kitchen faucet. Keep it under 120 words. Include the phrase "per our lease agreement" somewhere. Do not use the word "urgent". End the email with exactly the sign-off "Best regards," on its own line followed by nothing else. Keep the tone firm but polite.

constraints.text: Contains the phrase "per our lease agreement"
Ends with the sign-off "Best regards," and nothing after it
Tone is firm but polite (asks clearly for the repair without being rude or apologetic)
Reads as a complete email (greeting and body present, coherent request)

prompt: Explain why airplane windows are round instead of square, for a curious 10-year-old. Use exactly 3 paragraphs. Do not use the words "stress" or "fatigue". Include one everyday comparison a child would recognize. Keep the whole thing under 200 words.

constraints.text: Includes an everyday comparison a child would recognize
Explanation is accessible to a 10-year-old and factually correct about why round windows are safer

prompt: I have a free Saturday in Seattle with a $60 budget, no car, and I love books and coffee. Plan my day as a numbered list of exactly 5 stops in chronological order. For each stop give an estimated cost so the total stays under $60. Do not include any chain coffee shops (no Starbucks). Make the route walkable or transit-friendly in the order given.

constraints.text: Every stop has an estimated cost and the stated costs total under $60
Stops fit the stated interests (books and coffee feature prominently)
The route order is geographically sensible without a car

prompt: Explain the difference between a process and a thread to a junior developer. Structure your answer with exactly these two markdown headers in this order: "## What's shared" and "## What's separate". Under 180 words total. Include one concrete debugging symptom that tells you a bug is thread-related rather than process-related. Do not use the word "lightweight".

constraints.text: Has the two required headers in order
Includes a concrete debugging symptom distinguishing thread bugs

prompt: My small bakery's revenue is flat but foot traffic is up 20% this quarter. List exactly 4 plausible explanations as bullet points (using "-"), ordered from easiest to hardest to check. For each, name the one piece of data I should look at to confirm or rule it out. Do not suggest raising prices. Keep it under 160 words.

constraints.text: Each bullet names a specific piece of data to check
Explanations are ordered easiest-to-hardest to verify

prompt: Write a product description for a fictional umbrella that never inverts in wind. Exactly 2 paragraphs. The first paragraph must start with the word "Finally". Mention a specific wind speed it survives. Do not use the words "revolutionary" or "game-changer". Aim it at commuters, not hikers.

constraints.text: Clearly targets commuters rather than outdoor/hiking use

prompt: Draft a short LinkedIn post announcing that I'm leaving my job at a mid-size accounting firm after 6 years to start freelancing. Under 100 words. No hashtags. No emoji. Do not name the firm. Strike a tone that is grateful about the past but confident about the move, without any humble-bragging cliches like "I'm humbled" or "thrilled to announce".

constraints.text: Does not contain the phrase "thrilled to announce"
Tone is grateful about the past and confident about the future, without humble-brag cliches
Does not invent or name a firm

prompt: Answer in valid JSON only, with keys "summary", "pros", and "cons": should a family of four in a rainy city buy a second car or rely on one car plus transit and rideshare? "summary" is one sentence; "pros" and "cons" are arrays of exactly 3 short strings each, arguing for and against the second car. No text outside the JSON.

constraints.text: Has exactly the keys summary, pros, cons with pros/cons arrays of length 3
Summary is a single sentence taking a clear position
Pros and cons are substantive and non-overlapping

prompt: Give me a 4-week plan to go from zero running to finishing a 5K, as exactly 4 bullet points (one per week, using "-"). Each bullet must name the number of running days that week. Include exactly one rest-related question for me to consider, phrased as a question. Under 150 words. Do not mention any brand of shoe or app.

constraints.text: Each week's bullet states the number of running days
Progression is sensible for a true beginner (no sudden jumps)

prompt: My Python script reads a 2GB CSV and runs out of memory on a laptop with 8GB RAM. Explain what's likely happening and give exactly 3 numbered fixes in increasing order of implementation effort. Do not recommend buying more RAM or using a cloud VM. Under 170 words. Assume pandas is currently being used and say explicitly whether each fix keeps pandas.

constraints.text: Does not recommend buying RAM or cloud VMs
Fixes are ordered by increasing implementation effort
Each fix states whether pandas is kept
Diagnosis of the memory blowup is technically plausible

prompt: Compare buying versus leasing a car for someone who drives 8,000 miles a year and keeps cars a long time. Structure with exactly these headers in order: "## Buy", "## Lease", "## Verdict". The verdict must commit to one option for this specific driver and give the single strongest reason. Under 200 words. Do not use the phrase "it depends".

constraints.text: Has the three required headers in order
Does not use the phrase "it depends"
Verdict commits to one option for this driver profile
Reasoning actually uses the stated profile (low mileage, long ownership)

prompt: Write a 6-line poem about a traffic jam from the point of view of the road itself. Exactly 6 lines. The word "patience" must appear. No rhyming couplets (adjacent lines must not rhyme). End the final line with the word "home".

constraints.text: Point of view is recognizably the road's, not a driver's

prompt: Write a one-paragraph bio for a conference program for Dr. Maya Chen, a marine biologist who studies coral reef recovery and previously worked as a high school teacher for 5 years. Third person. Under 90 words. Must mention both the coral research and the teaching background. Do not use the words "passionate" or "expert".

constraints.text: Mentions both coral reef research and the teaching background

prompt: Why does my phone battery drain faster in cold weather? Answer in exactly 2 paragraphs: the first explains the chemistry in plain terms, the second gives practical advice. Under 160 words total. Include one specific temperature (any unit). Do not tell me to buy a new phone or battery.

constraints.text: First paragraph is chemistry, second is practical advice (in that order)
Does not recommend buying a new phone or battery
Chemistry explanation is correct in plain terms

prompt: Plan a 30-minute weekly team retrospective agenda for a 6-person remote team, as exactly 4 numbered agenda items with a minute allocation each (allocations must sum to 30). One item must be about appreciating a teammate. Do not include icebreakers. Under 130 words.

constraints.text: Minute allocations are present and sum to 30

prompt: A junior engineer asks: "Why did my SQL query get slow after the table grew to 10 million rows?" Give the 3 most likely causes as bullet points (using "-"), each with the one-line diagnostic query or command to confirm it. Under 150 words. Do not mention any specific database vendor by name.

constraints.text: Does not name a specific database vendor
Each bullet includes a concrete diagnostic query/command
The three causes are among the genuinely most likely (e.g. missing index, stale statistics, plan change)

prompt: I got two job offers: one pays $15K more but has a 55-minute commute; the other is 10 minutes away. Both jobs are otherwise similar. Walk me through the decision in exactly 3 paragraphs. Somewhere, convert the commute difference into hours per year and state the number. Do not tell me which one to pick. End with exactly one question I should ask myself.

constraints.text: Converts the commute difference into hours per year with an explicit number
Does not tell the reader which offer to pick
The hours-per-year arithmetic is approximately correct for a ~45-minute one-way difference

prompt: Write the opening paragraph of a mystery novel set in a 24-hour laundromat. One paragraph, under 110 words. It must start with the sentence "The dryers never stopped." Introduce exactly one named character. Do not reveal any crime yet — only atmosphere and unease.

constraints.text: No crime revealed; mood is atmospheric unease

prompt: Write a polite decline to a vendor's meeting request, by email. Under 80 words. Give a reason without inventing specifics (no fake deadlines or fake projects). Leave the door open for next quarter. Do not apologize more than once. Do not use the word "unfortunately".

constraints.text: Gives a reason without inventing specific fake details
Explicitly leaves the door open for next quarter

prompt: Explain inflation to someone who just got their first paycheck, using a grocery store as the running example throughout. Exactly 2 paragraphs, under 150 words. Include one specific percentage as an illustrative rate. Do not mention central banks, interest rates, or money printing.

constraints.text: Grocery store example is used throughout, not just once
Avoids central banks and money printing as instructed

prompt: Review this design decision for a to-do list app: "We store each user's tasks as one big JSON blob in a single database column." Give your assessment in exactly these sections, in order: "## Fine for now", "## Will hurt later", "## The one change I'd make today". Under 190 words total. The last section must recommend exactly one change.

constraints.text: Has the three required headers in order

value: ## The one change I'd make today

constraints.text: Last section recommends exactly one change
Trade-off analysis is technically sound (e.g. concurrency, partial updates, querying)
Acknowledges what is genuinely fine about the blob approach

prompt: My website's bounce rate dropped from 60% to 35% in one week with no releases. As bullet points (using "-"), list exactly 4 explanations ranked from most to least likely, and mark exactly one bullet with "[CHECK FIRST]" at the start. At least one explanation must be a measurement artifact rather than real user behavior. Under 140 words.

constraints.text: Exactly one bullet carries the [CHECK FIRST] marker
At least one explanation is a measurement/tracking artifact

prompt: Write a haiku sequence — exactly 3 haiku, separated by blank lines — about the last bus of the night. Traditional 5-7-5 syllable structure. The word "night" must appear somewhere in the sequence. The word "empty" may appear at most once across all three. The final haiku must contain a light source of some kind.

constraints.text: Exactly 3 stanzas separated by blank lines
"empty" appears at most once in total
Final haiku contains a light source

prompt: I'm hosting 8 people for dinner on a Friday after work; I get home at 5:30pm and guests arrive at 7pm. Plan the 90 minutes as exactly 5 numbered steps with clock times (e.g. "5:30–5:45"). The menu must require no oven (stovetop and cold dishes only). Include exactly one step that can be delegated to an early-arriving guest. Under 160 words.

constraints.text: Every step has clock times and they fit within 5:30–7:00 without overlap errors
Exactly one step is marked as delegable to a guest

prompt: Write the "About" section for a neighborhood tool-lending library's website. One paragraph, 60–100 words (both bounds matter). Must contain the phrase "borrow, don't buy". Mention that membership is free. Do not use the word "community" more than once. Warm but not saccharine.

constraints.text: Uses "community" at most once; tone warm but not saccharine

prompt: A friend says "I read that coffee is good for you one week and bad for you the next — nutrition science is useless." Respond in under 170 words. Acknowledge what's legitimate in their frustration before pushing back. Explain one concrete reason nutrition findings flip-flop (your choice), using plain language. Do not use the terms "confounder", "p-value", or "meta-analysis". End with exactly one question inviting them to keep talking.

constraints.text: Acknowledges the legitimate part of the frustration before disagreeing
Gives one concrete, correctly-explained reason findings flip-flop, in plain language
Avoids the other banned jargon (p-value, meta-analysis)

prompt: Answer in valid JSON only with keys "diagnosis", "quick_fix", "real_fix": my web page loads fast on WiFi but takes 8+ seconds on mobile data. "diagnosis" is one sentence naming the most likely cause; "quick_fix" is something deployable today; "real_fix" is the structural solution. Each value under 30 words. No text outside the JSON.

constraints.text: Has exactly the keys diagnosis, quick_fix, real_fix
Diagnosis is plausible for the WiFi-fast/cellular-slow symptom (e.g. payload size, no CDN)
quick_fix is genuinely deployable in a day; real_fix is structural

prompt: Rank these four ways to learn a language for a busy adult who can spare 30 min/day: apps, group classes, one-on-one tutoring, watching TV with subtitles. Present as exactly 4 numbered items, best first. For each: one sentence of justification tied to the 30-min/day constraint. Declare exactly one item "overrated" using that word. Under 150 words.

constraints.text: Exactly one item is called overrated
All four given methods are ranked (none dropped, none added)

prompt: Write a two-sentence horror story about a smart home assistant. Exactly 2 sentences. The first sentence must be mundane and comforting. The word "listening" must appear. No violence or gore — the horror must be implication only.

constraints.text: First sentence is mundane and comforting
No violence or gore; horror by implication

prompt: My 68-year-old mother is getting her first smartphone next week. Make a checklist of exactly 6 bullet points (using "-") for her first day with it, ordered by priority. One bullet must be about scam/phishing awareness. Do not mention any specific phone brand or carrier. Under 140 words. Tone: practical, not condescending.

constraints.text: Tone is practical and not condescending
